name: babl
desc: Dynamic, any-to-any, pixel format translation library
why: Any-to-any pixel format translation from GEGL; a clever transform layer, though it is mostly plumbing under GIMP.

brief.what_it_is: babl is a C library that converts pixel data between pixel formats, covering different bit depths, data types, color models, color spaces, and component orders. You describe a source format and a destination format, and babl builds a "fish" (a conversion object) for that pair. You then run the fish over a buffer of pixels to get converted output. New formats can be composed from registered color models and data types, and new conversions can be added as shared-object extensions. The homepage describes babl as a pixel encoding and color space conversion engine.
brief.why_it_exists: The page frames babl as the engine behind GEGL's GeglBuffer, which stores image tiles and converts pixel data implicitly through babl formats, so GIMP can handle many pixel layouts without each one needing a hand-written converter. It is pitched both at GIMP itself and at other software that wants pixel format or color space conversion.
brief.how_it_works: Conversions are built from a reference implementation in 64-bit floating point, with fast paths (SIMD and lookup tables) registered as shortcuts that babl can use as intermediate steps when it assembles a fish. Runtime profiling and validation pick the code path, and the results are cached and persisted across runs. Color spaces can be created from chromaticity coordinates or ICC v2/v4 profiles, and the page says unified-alpha conversion avoids the precision loss that comes from dividing by zero alpha when moving between separate and associated alpha.

commands_seen.context: Clones the main babl git repository, hosted by GNOME; the page says it can also be browsed online there.

brief.install_notes: The homepage gives no build instructions beyond the git clone. The news section mentions a meson build (its release notes cite meson 0.54 as a dependency) and says babl can be used as a subproject in other meson projects. Optional lcms2 is needed for CMYK ICC profiles. Runtime configuration is through environment variables: BABL_TOLERANCE sets the speed/accuracy trade-off (default 0.000001; 0.01 to 0.1 is suggested for preview), and BABL_PATH gives the directory where extension .so files are loaded from. Releases are published at download.gimp.org/pub/babl/.
brief.standout: Any-to-any conversion is built on a small set of primitives: formats are assembled from registered color models and data types, and babl chooses an optimal chain of conversions, using fast-path shortcuts as intermediate steps, instead of storing a converter for every pair. The page also states a clear design rule that the 64-bit reference conversions govern correctness of any extension.
brief.status: Maintained, as far as the homepage shows. The most recent news entry is babl-0.1.116 on 2025-10-02, and earlier releases are dated 2025-05-08, 2025-03-10 and 2024-09-27, so releases are steady. I did not check the git log, so the latest commit date is unknown.
brief.caveats: Per the page's TODO list, spectral pixel formats and datatypes that are not a multiple of 8 bits are not yet implemented, and many SIMD variants for more architectures are still missing. The news says LUT code paths are disabled on big-endian systems. CMYK ICC support needs the lcms2 dependency. Licensed under LGPL v3 or later. The page is a project homepage, not a reference manual. The cli tool named in the executables list is only mentioned in the news ("add commandline tool"), and the page shows no usage for it.
quotes: babl is pixel encoding and color space conversion engine in C.
Dynamically extendable with new formats, color models, components and datatypes, and SIMD code paths.
Most users of babl do not know they are using babl and it is GIMP itself which uses babl
